Do your self a big favour and take your watch to a reputable repairer in the city you will save a bundle. I took a Seiko watch in to be appraised for repair. I was told the appraisal would cost $45. Prior to agreeing, I requested a price on a straight swap of the mechanism, this is a very easy straight forward job. Movement swaps are regularly performed on older model seiko watches and easily priced, the lady at the counter said she was unable to provide a price for a straight swap of the mechanism (this should have raised alarm bells) and that the watch needed to be assessed. After a couple of days I received a quote via email for a straight swap of the mechanism for $495 which is outrageous given the mechanisms retail for between $90 - $130.
I returned to the shop to pick up the watch having received 3 quotes for the same job ranging from $200 to $280 (no assessment charge). Upon pickup I asked the result of the assessment, there had been no assessment of the existing movement, the only thing that had been done to “assess” the watch was to have the case back unscrewed and the existing movement identified, the watch maker was unable to identify any fault with the movement as it had not been examined, this “assessment” would have taken under 1 minute and a reputable repairer would usually do this on the spot for free. The moral of this story is if you are unfamiliar with what is reasonable and what is not, join a facebook watch enthusiasts group and seek their assistance and obtain a recommendation to a reputable watch repairer, one that is familiar with the type of watch you wish to have restored or repaired.I would not recommend “A Watch In Time” I was charged for an assessment of my watch that I did not receive there was no intention at all to repair the watch it was never going to be anything else than a movement swap and their pricing was nothing less than a rip off.

Very disappointing experience — over-promised and under-delivered.
We engaged this immigration lawyer because we were extremely busy and did not have the time to research the visa process and prepare everything ourselves. We trusted that, by paying a professional, we would receive proper advice, guidance and a thorough assessment of our circumstances.
Unfortunately, our experience was the opposite. From our initial discussions, the process was made to sound very simple and as though we did not need much supporting evidence. Based on the advice we received, we genuinely believed our application was being prepared appropriately.
We were particularly disappointed to later discover that the visa application had been lodged under what we believe was the wrong visa category — the Sponsored Family stream, despite the applicant not being a family member of the sponsor in the way required for that category. This is exactly the type of issue we relied on a professional immigration adviser to identify and advise us about before lodging.
Our application was subsequently refused. We completely understand that no immigration lawyer or migration agent can guarantee a visa outcome, and we would never blame an agent simply because an application was unsuccessful. Our issue is the level of advice and preparation we received beforehand.
What was even more frustrating was that after the refusal, we were told that we could reapply with additional evidence. However, this additional evidence was not properly requested from us before the original application was lodged and decided. If this evidence could potentially have strengthened the application, we believe we should have been advised about it and given the opportunity to provide it beforehand.
The email we received after the refusal also stated that the required services had been completed in full and to a professional standard. From our perspective, however, we felt that the service amounted to little more than completing and lodging the application. We expected much more proactive advice, particularly regarding the appropriate visa pathway, potential concerns with the application and the evidence needed to address those concerns.
We engaged a professional precisely because we didn't have the time or expertise to do this ourselves. Unfortunately, we were left feeling that we could have achieved a similar result by doing the application ourselves, while having to pay for professional assistance.
In our experience, she over-promised and under-delivered. The way the process was explained to us initially gave us confidence that everything was straightforward and that we didn't need to do very much. The eventual outcome and the lack of preparation for the issues raised by the Department were extremely disappointing.
We would strongly encourage anyone considering using this service to make sure they independently understand the visa category, eligibility requirements and supporting evidence needed before relying entirely on the advice provided by Lawanya.
Based on our personal experience, we would not recommend this company.
